problem_statement: The IEEE 802.15.4 frame parser and its information-element parser must reject malformed, truncated, and oversized received frames and information elements, while parsing well-formed frames and a valid TSCH channel-hopping-sequence information element correctly. From the perspective of a caller or test that hands these parsers exact-length byte buffers and inspects their return value and the parsed result: (1) a data frame whose frame-control field advertises long destination/source addressing and a security header but supplies only the frame-control bytes, or only the sequence number and destination PAN ID and is then cut off inside the destination address, is parsed as successful (a header length is returned) instead of being rejected; (2) a frame whose security-control octet has its reserved high bit set is parsed into the wrong result, so the reported header length and the stored security-control fields do not match the input; (3) an information element whose declared length exceeds the buffer, an information element with zero length, and a channel-hopping-sequence sub-element shorter than its fixed header are accepted instead of being rejected, and a sequence length is stored even though the sub-element was never fully copied; (4) a well-formed short-addressed data frame, and a complete valid channel-hopping-sequence information element, must still parse and yield the correct fields (sequence number, frame type, hopping-sequence id, length and list). The required behavior is that all of the malformed, truncated, and oversized inputs return the documented failure value and leave stored state untouched, while the well-formed frames and the valid hopping-sequence element parse correctly.
causal_chain: The upstream negative-path scenario builds the framer together with the new test source and feeds it a series of exact-length byte arrays, asserting each parser's return value and stored fields. The malformed vectors (a frame advertising a large header but only a few bytes present, a security-control octet with the reserved bit set, an information element whose length exceeds the buffer, a zero-length element, and a channel-hopping-sequence sub-element shorter than its fixed header) are asserted to be rejected, and the well-formed frame and a valid hopping-sequence element are asserted to parse with the correct fields. Under the base code these malformed inputs are accepted (a non-zero / positive return and/or unvalidated stored state) so the rejection assertions fail, while the post-fix code returns the failure value and leaves stored state untouched, so the same assertions pass; the JS runner observes the FAILED marker before the fix and the DONE marker after it.

superseded_statements.problem_statement: The IEEE 802.15.4 frame parser accepts and processes received frames that are shorter than, or malformed relative to, the header and information elements they advertise, on the unauthenticated receive path where every length field is attacker-controlled. A truncated frame whose header flags declare long addressing plus a security header, but that supplies only the header flags, is not rejected and the parser reads far past the supplied buffer. Malformed information elements are accepted as valid rather than rejected: a 6top payload element with a zero length, a TSCH channel-hopping-sequence element shorter than its fixed header, and an element declaring more bytes than remain in the buffer all pass through. When a frame's security-control octet sets bits reserved by the specification, the parser misreads the frame-counter control bits, skips the frame counter, and consumes the wrong header length. The parsers must instead validate that enough input is present before each field access and reject any frame or information element whose declared length exceeds the remaining input, returning the documented failure value and leaving no unvalidated state behind, while still accepting well-formed frames and a valid hopping-sequence element.
check_issues: `problem_statement` gives the fix away: "The parsers must instead validate that enough input is present before each field access and reject any frame or information element whose declared length exceeds the remaining input, returning the documented failure value and leaving no unvalidated state behind, while still accepting well-formed frames and a valid hopping-sequence element.". Describe only the observable symptom, its trigger and the required behavior, not what the code checks or must do internally
